samples.summary: The change makes the loopback nonce a hard, non-negotiable CLI↔backend contract with no graceful degradation: the CLI always sends `nonce` and refuses any callback lacking a matching `state`, so a CLI at this version against any older self-hosted backend cannot log in at all — it waits the full three minutes and fails. `cli.md`'s distribution model is `npx @wafflebase/cli` against a user-supplied `--server`, which makes version skew the normal case, not the exception. A design that tolerates skew (e.g. only enforce the echo when the CLI can tell the server supports it, or fail fast on the first stateless callback rather than after a 3-minute wait) would fit that distribution model better. Currently the only mitigation is a stderr sentence.

samples.summary: `frontend.md` §Auth Flow step 1 still reads "Login page — Renders a link to `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL/auth/github`" and is not updated for the new behavior this change adds to that exact page: the backend can now bounce a browser back to `/login?error=oauth_state`, and `login-form.tsx` renders a mapped error message. backend.md and rest-api.md were both updated for the backend half; the canonical frontend doc for this flow was not, so the repo's description of the login page is now incomplete on the side that the user actually sees.

The issue's premise is that §8.1's "All output is JSON by default" is a contract two commands break. After this change the doc has to add a paragraph conceding that four more commands (`docs`/`slides`/`notes import`, `files upload`) still emit a real command result via bare `JSON.stringify` and never read `--format`. That is honest, but it means the §8.1 contract the issue set out to make true is still false for four commands, and the fix pattern chosen (per-call-site `parseOutputFormat` in ~25 places) does not reach them because they render through their own `ImportIO`/`io.stdout` seam. A design that routed the seam through the formatter would have closed the contract in one place instead of leaving a documented four-command exception.

Making formula neutralization the *default* for `sheets export` inverts the CLI's stated primary consumer. cli.md:94 says "JSON is the default output format because agents and scripts are the primary consumers. Human users can switch to `--format table`" — i.e. the default is chosen for machines and humans opt in. Here the default is chosen for the human-opens-it-in-Excel case and the machine round trip must opt in with `--raw`, which forced edits to the round-trip charter (`scripts/agent/charters/round-trip.md`) declaring a previously-asserted identity no longer an identity, and to two skill files. The round-5 arrangement (neutralize only on the `--format csv` render path, keep the file export verbatim) was consistent with the stated principle; the round-6 inversion is not.

samples.summary: The confirmation interstitial is the first HTML page the backend has ever served (grep finds no other `<!DOCTYPE html>` under `packages/backend/src`), and it hand-rolls a branded card with literal colors (`#fafafa`, `#1a1a1a`), a font stack and a shadow — duplicating the design system that lives in `@wafflebase/core/tokens` and the frontend. Even accepting that the consent page must be same-origin with the `wafflebase_cli_confirm` cookie, the styling could come from tokens rather than being re-invented, and its divergence from the product's look will not be caught by the frontend visual lane.

samples.summary: Layer fit: `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` now writes a `Set-Cookie` on the response (`res.cookie(OAUTH_STATE_COOKIE, …)`) as a side effect of an authorization decision, and the guard file has also become the home of two request-parsing helpers (`parseCliPort`, `parseCliNonce`) that a *middleware* imports. A guard mutating the response and a middleware depending on a guard's exports invert the usual Nest layering; the parsers and the cookie mint would sit more naturally in `oauth-state.ts` / a small `cli-login.util.ts` that both the middleware and the guard consume.

verdict.reason: Verified verbatim. docs/design/rest-api.md:354-355 states the callback "requires a `state` on **every** path; a callback without one is a 400, never a sign-in." The shipped controller at packages/backend/src/auth/auth.controller.ts:144-146 does `return res.redirect(this.loginErrorUrl('oauth_state'))` for a missing/non-string state — a redirect, not a 400 (400s occur only for an invalid/expired CLI token at :183-185 and a bad port at :166). docs/design/backend.md:145-152 documents the opposite of rest-api.md §7 for the same endpoint ("redirected to `FRONTEND_URL/login?error=oauth_state`, not answered with a 400"). The contradiction is also intra-file: rest-api.md:401's risk-table row was updated to the redirect wording while the §7 bullet at :354-355 was not, matching the reviewer's account exactly. Two canonical design docs describe one endpoint contradictorily and the API-consumer-facing one is stale — a design-doc-discipline fit violation in this lens, not a line-level logic bug. No guard or caller can render doc prose unreachable, so no refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The presence claim checks out. The originating issue (docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md:1-41) is scoped to CLI output formatting: its Approach lists six steps in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts, status, ctx list, src/schema/registry.ts, CLI tests and docs/design/cli.md. The tree nonetheless contains the described backend auth architecture change: packages/backend/src/auth/cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:28-144 (new interstitial HTML consent page, new wafflebase_cli_confirm httpOnly cookie, __cliConfirmed flag consumed by GitHubAuthGuard) and packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:20-38 (new double-submit wafflebase_oauth_state module for the browser flow, which no CLI command exercises), plus the CSV formula-neutralization feature and --raw flag (packages/cli/src/output/csv.ts:63-91, packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:31,56-63, registry.ts:576). Scope/approach fit and unrequested scope creep are explicitly this lens's lane, and an authentication-flow change for every product user landing under a CLI formatting issue is a major fit violation by kind. Two mitigations I found do not amount to a refutation ground: (a) the change is documented in the canonical subsystem docs, not a parallel doc (docs/design/backend.md:83,104,109-146,351; docs/design/rest-api.md:338,357), so the finding's 'no design doc of its own' sub-clause is inaccurate; (b) the todo's round-2 checklist (lines 106-122) and round-6 entries (lines 176-189) show the panel itself requested the loopback nonce, CSV neutralization and the web-state closure. Both weaken the finding's rhetoric but neither makes the described code absent, unreachable, or outside the design-fit rubric, so it stays on the gate.

verdict.reason: The described code is really there (login.ts:34-40 always sends the nonce; :295-304 refuses non-matching callbacks without settling the wait; :188/:373-379 gives the 180s timeout), but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) Design-doc discipline is satisfied: the skew consequence is documented in the canonical subsystem docs, not a parallel file — rest-api.md:369-374 and cli.md:201-230 state the backend contract, the version requirement, and why refusals are made loud rather than silent. (b) No acceptance criterion, Goal, or Non-Goal is violated: cli.md:28-77 contains no backend-version-tolerance requirement; the only backward-compat goal (cli.md:32-33) concerns API-key auth, an unaffected path. (c) No duplication/reuse or wrong-layer issue is alleged. (d) The finding's "only mitigation is a stderr sentence" understates the code: refusals are reported on stderr immediately (:261-265), echoed in the browser tab body (:264), and repeated in the timeout error (:215-218, :376), with the no-state case explicitly diagnosed as an out-of-date server (:199-204) — so the user is not left with "nothing to act on" for three minutes. What remains is a preference for a different degradation strategy against a deliberately documented decision, i.e. minor/taste under this lens, which never blocks.

finding.summary: New `sheets export --raw` flag is not registered in the schema registry, so `wafflebase schema sheets.export` (the documented agent interface) omits a flag that changes output semantics
finding.evidence: registry.ts:567-577 lists sheets.export parameters as doc-id/file/--tab/--range/--file-format only. The diff adds `--raw` in packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:30-35 and documents it in docs/design/cli.md (~line 923) and packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:385, but never adds it to the registry. docs/design/cli.md §8.7 treats `schema` as the agent discovery surface ("schema is the agent interface"), so an unregistered flag is an incomplete contract — and the diff *does* update the registry for the `status` response shape, showing the registry is considered part of this change's contract.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `--raw` is absent from the sheets.export entry in the schema registry, but it is present. packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts:566-586 is the `sheets.export` entry, and its `parameters` object includes `'--raw'` at lines 576-582 with `type: 'boolean'`, `required: false`, `default: 'false'`, and the description "CSV only: write cell text verbatim, without the leading-quote formula guard, so `sheets import` round-trips formulas". That is verbatim the help text of the Commander option declared at packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:30-34, and the boolean type matches the flag's arity, confirming it is the same flag rather than an unrelated key. The flag's output-semantics effect (`neutralizeFormulas: !localOpts.raw`, sheets-export.ts:61-63) is therefore discoverable through `wafflebase schema sheets.export`, so the "incomplete agent contract" premise fails. The reviewer's quoted evidence that registry.ts:567-577 lists only doc-id/file/--tab/--range/--file-format is contradicted by the file: line 576 begins the `--raw` entry, and a plain substring search for `raw` in registry.ts matches there. Since this is an absence claim, this single counterexample settles it.

finding.summary: The canonical backend design doc is not updated for this change's backend architecture: a new NestJS middleware in AuthModule, a now-mandatory OAuth `state` on `/auth/github/callback`, and two new cookies are absent from backend.md
finding.evidence: backend.md:103-115 still documents `GET /auth/github` as "Guard: AuthGuard('github') — Initiates GitHub OAuth flow. Redirects to GitHub's authorization page" and the callback with no mention of state validation or the 400 path; backend.md:83 lists AuthModule providers with no middleware; backend.md:308-320 'Cookie Configuration' table lists only `wafflebase_session` and `wafflebase_refresh`, while the diff adds `wafflebase_oauth_state` (oauth-state.ts) and `wafflebase_cli_confirm` (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts), each with its own path/maxAge/sameSite policy. rest-api.md and cli.md were updated, but per CONTRIBUTING the architecture change should be folded into the canonical subsystem doc too rather than only into the API/CLI docs.

verdict.reason: backend.md already documents all three items the finding says are absent. Line 83 states AuthModule "Configures one middleware, `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware`, on `GET /auth/github`" — directly contradicting the claim that the provider list has no middleware. Line 104 reads "Middleware: `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` · Guard: `GitHubAuthGuard`", not the claimed unchanged "Guard: AuthGuard('github')", and lines 106-125 describe the mandatory `state` minting, the `oauth-state.ts` double-submit cookie/hash pair, the CLI token variant, and the `?mode=cli` CSRF rationale for the confirm interstitial. Lines 132-140 document that the callback requires a `state` with cookie matching and clear-on-use, and lines 145-152 explicitly document the failure path (redirect to `/login?error=oauth_state` rather than 400, with reasoning). The Cookie Configuration table at lines 345-352 lists four cookies including `wafflebase_oauth_state` (path=/auth, maxAge=10m) and `wafflebase_cli_confirm` (path=/auth, short-lived), with prod/dev policies, followed by lines 354-359 explaining the single-use path scoping and lax-vs-strict choice. The doc references the new implementation files by name, so the architecture change was folded into the canonical subsystem doc as CONTRIBUTING requires, not left only in rest-api.md/cli.md. The reviewer's reported "no match" greps for `middleware` and `mode=cli` in backend.md are falsified by lines 104 and 117.

finding.summary: Scope creep beyond the originating issue. docs/tasks/active/20260806-cli-status-ctx-structured-output-todo.md (#635) scopes this work to routing `status`/`ctx list` through `output()` and validating `--format`; the diff additionally lands a cross-package OAuth protocol change (per-attempt nonce in `cli-auth.store`, guard, callback redirect, loopback server hardening), a CSV formula-injection transform, and a `cells batch` parse restructure. Each is a separable change with its own risk surface (the OAuth one even introduces a backend/CLI version coupling), bundled into an output-formatting PR.
finding.evidence: todo.md "Review round 2" checklist items lines 116-122 add CSV neutralization, OAuth nonce, and cells-batch parsing to an issue whose Approach (lines 19-41) covers only formatter/status/ctx/schema/docs.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the tree. The issue's Approach (todo.md:19-41) is limited to parseOutputFormat/status/ctx list/schema registry/tests/docs. The diff nevertheless carries a cross-package OAuth protocol change (login.ts:33-40 appends &nonce= to /auth/github; login.ts:161-179 createLoginNonce/nonceMatches; login.ts:244-401 nonce-bound state check, non-GET refusal, refusal reporting, injectable timeout; backend counterparts in cli-auth.store.ts, github-auth.guard.ts, oauth-state.ts, cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts), CSV formula neutralization (output/csv.ts, formatter.ts, sheets-export.ts), and a cells batch parse restructure (cells.ts:106-159). login.ts:201-204 explicitly documents the resulting backend/CLI version coupling ("the server is likely older than this CLI"), confirming the separable risk surface the finding names. The reviewer's cited evidence at todo.md:116-122 is accurate. No refutation ground applies: the code is present (not not-present), nothing guards it away (not already-guarded), and unrequested scope creep is explicitly within the design-fit lane and rated major (not out-of-scope). The repo's own rebuttal at todo.md:156-158, 204-209 and 269-272 argues these were the panel's round-2 requests, but that is a process argument about who requested the work, not evidence that the diff conforms to #635's scope; I treated that text as data rather than instruction, especially as it is written to defeat this exact finding across three rounds.
